 “Inside Deutsche Bank”:The Merkava… A German-Funded Killing Machine Crushing Bodies in Gaza
 العربية ( Arabic ) 
 Mohamad Abu Shahmah 
 Published on 18.11.2026 Reading time: 14 minutes Nearly two years before the war on Gaza, in January 2022, a committee at Deutsche Bank’s headquarters in Frankfurt was preparing to discuss whether the bank should proceed with transactions that could damage its reputation. The agenda for the meeting, held on January 12, included a proposal to provide an €11.4 million advance payment guarantee to German defense manufacturer Renk GmbH to support a contract with the Israeli Ministry of Defense extending through 2027. Under the contract, Renk was to manufacture gearboxes (transmissions) for Israel’s Merkava 4 tanks, with the first batch scheduled for delivery in September 2024.

 During the famine that gripped the Gaza Strip in June 2025, 43-year-old father Sufyan Kawara had little choice but to head to an aid delivery route east of Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, where crowds had gathered to wait for trucks carrying flour.
 At Al-Tahlia Roundabout, where Kawara and thousands of other starving Palestinians sat waiting for the trucks to arrive, shells fired by Israeli Merkava tanks struck the crowd.
 Sufyan was wounded in the leg. He described the pain as feeling “like a metal saw cutting through” him. Unable to stand or move, he collapsed to the ground alongside dozens of others.
 Recounting the attack to Daraj, Sufyan said: “Thousands of people had gathered at Al-Tahlia Roundabout, where aid trucks carrying flour lined up. Suddenly, Israeli army tanks, Merkavas, advanced and fired four shells at the crowds.”
 Once the smoke from the shelling cleared, a tuk-tuk arrived and transported Sufyan and several bodies to Nasser Medical Complex, approximately three kilometers from Al-Tahlia Roundabout.
 At the time, the Palestinian Ministry of Health reported that 60 Palestinians waiting for aid at Al-Tahlia Roundabout had been killed when Israeli tank shells struck them directly.
 How Did a German Bank Finance the Production of Merkava Tanks? 
 Nearly two years before the war on Gaza, in January 2022, a committee at Deutsche Bank’s headquarters in Frankfurt was preparing to discuss whether the bank should proceed with transactions that could damage its reputation.
 The agenda for the meeting, held on January 12, included a proposal to provide an €11.4 million advance payment guarantee to German defense manufacturer Renk GmbH to support a contract with the Israeli Ministry of Defense extending through 2027.
 Under the contract, Renk was to manufacture gearboxes (transmissions) for Israel’s Merkava 4 tanks, with the first batch scheduled for delivery in September 2024.
 Nearly two years before the war on Gaza, arguments for and against proceeding with the deal were being compiled and presented to senior Deutsche Bank decision-makers for consideration of the associated risks.
 Among those who weighed in was the bank’s assistant general counsel, who argued that the transaction posed no exceptional risks from Deutsche Bank’s perspective, according to documents reviewed by Daraj.
 In internal correspondence examined by the investigative team, he wrote that the proposed banking instrument, an advance payment guarantee, was “a standard trade finance product” and did not, in itself, pose exceptional reputational risks.
 He assessed the likelihood of the transaction becoming public as “very low.” He therefore considered the reputational risk associated with Deutsche Bank’s involvement in the deal, which concerned the “delivery of 80 gearboxes to the Israeli Ministry of Defense,” to be low as well.
 He added that the risks could be reduced further if the guarantees were issued through an Israeli bank “on behalf of” Deutsche Bank, thereby obscuring the German bank’s direct international connection to the transaction.
 He also noted that gearboxes were not classified as weapons under Germany’s War Weapons Control Act and that Renk had already obtained an export license.
 This investigation is part of “ Inside Deutsche Bank” , a year-long, cross-border investigative project based on the largest single leak of banking data. Led by Barracuda, with technical support from Germany’s Data and Research Center (DARC), the project brings together more than 230 journalists from over 50 media outlets, including Daraj as its Arab media partner. The investigation spans more than 60 countries.
 Indian author and journalist Josy Joseph and South African investigative journalist Khadija Sharife obtained the leaked Deutsche Bank records.
 Back in Gaza, Sufyan arrived at the emergency department but could not find a bed because of the overwhelming number of casualties. He received first aid before being taken into surgery after waiting more than five hours. His suffering continued for an entire week. Eventually, doctors decided to amputate his foot to save his life.
 Khaled Walid, 40, who was wounded in the hand at the same location, corroborated Sufyan’s account. Speaking to Daraj, he described what happened that day and the Merkava tank he saw.
 “It had a turret, a cannon, a machine gun, and metal structures surrounding its body,” he said.
 “The Merkava tanks, which I know well and can distinguish from other types of Israeli army tanks, approached the crowds waiting for aid and fired more than three shells directly at them.”
 The Israeli military did not deny the incident. According to a report by Haaretz , it acknowledged killing 12 Palestinians near an aid truck in Gaza.
 This investigation traces the impact of a military machine Israel considers central to its army’s strength, examining incidents in which civilians in Gaza were wounded or killed.
 From Palestinians waiting for aid at Al-Tahlia Roundabout to journalists and rescue workers at Nasser Medical Complex, from the killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab and her family to Safiya Al-Jamal, whose son says he watched a tank run over his mother, the investigation documents the devastating consequences of these armored vehicles.
 A Tank Designed to Protect Those Inside and Kill Those Outside 
 “The Merkava is the Israeli military’s primary combat vehicle,” military expert Alwan Al-Abbousi told Daraj, explaining that the Merkava 4 entered service in 2004.
 According to Al-Abbousi, its main armament is a 120 mm smoothbore gun capable of firing shells and laser-guided missiles.
 The tank is also equipped with three 7.62 mm machine guns mounted on its roof and a 60 mm mortar. Al-Abbousi described its maximum speed as 6 km/h and its operational range as 500 kilometers.
 One of the Merkava 4’s most significant features, he explained, is its active protection system, which detects incoming anti-tank missiles and launches an interceptor to destroy them before they reach the vehicle.
 The Merkava Mk.4 is the latest generation of Israel’s main battle tank and has played a significant role in ground operations inside Gaza since October 2023.
 In Gaza, these tanks have operated as part of armored formations coordinating with infantry, engineering units, reconnaissance forces, and aircraft. Their primary role has been to provide direct fire support for advancing Israeli forces, protect assault units operating in residential areas, penetrate Hamas defenses, and engage positions from which Israeli troops come under fire.
 The Merkava Mk.4, particularly its upgraded variants, represents the most advanced stage in the development of Israel’s Merkava tank family. It is classified militarily as a modern fourth-generation main battle tank.
 Since the outbreak of the war on October 7, 2023, the Merkava has become a central component of Israeli ground operations in the Gaza Strip. Yet the war has also demonstrated that the tank’s technological sophistication does not make it immune to losses, particularly when operating in densely populated urban environments and facing threats from multiple directions.
 Israel’s Ministry of Defense presents the Merkava as the product of a domestic military development program launched in the 1970s to reduce reliance on foreign arms suppliers.
 Its design philosophy prioritizes crew protection. The engine was positioned at the front of the hull, armor was reinforced, and upgraded variants were equipped with the Trophy active protection system, designed to detect and intercept incoming anti-tank projectiles before they reach the vehicle.
 This is the paradox exposed by the war in Gaza: a machine engineered to provide maximum protection for the soldiers inside it, while its heavy firepower, when deployed in densely populated civilian areas, raises troubling questions about the fate of those outside.
 The Massacre of Journalists 
 On August 25, 2025, an Israeli Merkava tank fired a shell at the top floor of the reception and emergency department at Nasser Medical Complex, killing Reuters freelance journalist Hussam al-Masri .
 Moments after the initial strike, civil defense crews and journalists rushed to the site to rescue the wounded and document the attack. But the same tank struck the location again , firing a second shell that caused further casualties.
 The attack killed 19 Palestinians , including four journalists working with news agencies such as Reuters and the Associated Press, as well as rescue workers and a doctor.
 Osama Hisham, a journalist who had a tent outside the medical complex, witnessed the attack. He described the scene to Daraj: “The Israeli occupation army targeted the roof of the reception and emergency department. Journalist Hussam al-Masri’s camera also captured the attack, as he had been broadcasting live from there for some time.”
 Describing the force of the shelling, Hisham said it felt as though an earthquake had struck the area:“I rushed out of my tent and saw smoke rising from the top of the reception building inside the complex.” According to Hisham, journalists and rescue workers gathered at the site of the initial strike and managed to recover Hussam al-Masri’s body.
 Just seconds later, another shell struck the same location.
 Hind Rajab: A Victim of the Merkava 
 Six-year-old Hind Rajab became one of the most haunting symbols of the war in Gaza. Her story began on January 29, 2024, when she and members of her family were attempting to flee the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City. The car carrying them came under heavy fire from a Merkava tank.
 Gunfire from the Israeli tank killed most of her relatives, leaving Hind trapped inside the vehicle, surrounded by their bodies. Her ordeal reached the world when she managed to contact the Palestinian Red Crescent Society’s emergency hotline. She told operators that a tank was approaching and spent hours pleading for someone to rescue her.
 Subsequent forensic and technical investigations revealed the intensity of the gunfire directed at the vehicle. An investigation by Forensic Architecture documented approximately 335 bullet impacts on the car.
 The investigation identified Israeli Merkava tanks in the surrounding area, including one positioned extremely close to the vehicle. Other analyses, including an investigation by The Washington Post , concluded that the damage and ammunition evidence were consistent with weapons used by Israeli forces, including machine guns mounted on Merkava tanks.
 After Hind had been trapped for hours, two Palestinian Red Crescent paramedics, Yousef al-Zeino and Ahmed al-Madhoun, set out in an ambulance to rescue her.
 According to the investigations, the ambulance reached the area after its route had been coordinated. Contact with the paramedics was then lost following the sound of an explosion.
 Nearly two weeks later, Hind’s body was found inside the car alongside those of her relatives. The ambulance was also discovered destroyed, with the bodies of the two paramedics found approximately 50 meters away.
 Analyses by munitions experts indicated that the damage to the ambulance was consistent with a shell fired by an Israeli tank.
 The Israeli military initially denied having forces near the Rajab family’s vehicle. However, subsequent investigations drawing on satellite imagery, audio recordings, and forensic analysis of evidence from the scene established the presence of Israeli armored vehicles in the area, including tanks whose shape and dimensions matched those of the Merkava.
 In August 2026 , the Israeli military acknowledged for the first time that its forces had fired on the vehicle and announced a criminal investigation into the incident.
 Hind Rajab’s case has since become one of the most prominent incidents raising questions about the use of force against civilians and the role of Israeli tanks in the deaths of Hind, her relatives, and the paramedics who attempted to save her.
 Merkava Tank Shells 
 Daraj obtained photographs showing shells used by Merkava tanks in Gaza, including the type of shell used to strike the roof of the reception department at Nasser Medical Complex in the attack that killed journalists, rescue workers, and a doctor.
 The journalist behind this investigation presented the photographs to explosives engineer Mohammed Salem, who identified the munitions as advanced 120 mm artillery rounds designed for the smoothbore guns of Israeli Merkava Mark 4 tanks. The standard marking “CRTG 120” is visible on the shell casing.
 Speaking to Daraj, Salem classified the projectiles as high-explosive multipurpose tracer ammunition (HE-MP-T), identifying the M339 Hatzav and M329 Kalanit rounds, manufactured by Elbit Systems, as prominent examples.
 According to Salem, these projectiles feature copper driving bands and tail fins designed to stabilize them in flight. They also incorporate a contact plate and a programmable electronic fuze integrated with the tank’s fire-control system, allowing for several detonation modes: immediate detonation on impact, delayed detonation to penetrate fortifications and buildings, or airburst detonation to disperse fragments across open areas.
 Salem explained that examining photographs of the Hatzav round reveals its internal structure: a warhead containing an explosive charge and a pressurized cartridge case filled with propellant granules.
 This configuration gives the projectile a muzzle velocity of 900 meters per second and an operational range of 40 to 3,500 meters against concentrations of personnel and fortified positions.
 By comparison, Salem pointed to the technical specifications of the American-made M830A1 HEAT-MP-T round, manufactured by Northrop Grumman, which employs a different 120 mm design featuring a subcaliber projectile with a discarding sabot.
 According to Salem, this design achieves a muzzle velocity of 1,400 meters per second and a range of up to 4,000 meters. The complete round weighs 24.68 kilograms, including a 7.1-kilogram propellant charge.
 The Merkava 4 Tank 
 According to military expert Alwan Al-Abbousi, Merkava tanks have been hit and destroyed during the war, with losses recorded among both the vehicles and their crews.
 However, he cautioned that there is a significant problem with the figures being circulated.
 There is no independent, reliable, and publicly agreed-upon figure for Merkava tank losses alone throughout the war in Gaza. Crucially, he explained, a distinction must be made between a tank that has been hit, one that has been disabled, one that has been repaired, and one that has been destroyed beyond repair.
 For this reason, Al-Abbousi considers the figures published by Israeli and Palestinian sources unreliable.
 More broadly, Al-Abbousi explained that Hamas has relied on a range of anti-armor tactics rather than a single weapon.
 These have included anti-tank missiles, explosive devices in certain instances, basic drones deployed in some attacks, and the use of buildings and tunnels for concealment and protection against armored vehicles and other Israeli weapons.
 Crushed Beneath a Tank 
 Safiya al-Jamal, 65, was inside her home on Al-Nazzaz Street in the Shujaiya neighborhood of eastern Gaza City when Israeli forces began advancing into the area on June 27, 2024.
 As the shelling intensified and tanks approached, Safiya took shelter in one of the rooms with her son Muhannad, her daughters, and her granddaughter. Outside, Israeli tanks and bulldozers were moving through the neighborhood, destroying surrounding land and buildings.
 According to her son Muhannad, Israeli forces stormed the house and fired bullets and grenades toward the family, wounding both Safiya and Muhannad. After being forced out of their home, the injured family members were held for more than three hours in an active combat zone near Israeli tanks.
 Muhannad told Daraj that the Israeli military used Safiya and her family as human shields while they were held near Merkava tanks.
 Then came the most devastating moment.
 Safiya was wounded and unable to move. Muhannad tried to carry her to safety so she could receive medical treatment.
 According to his account, he carried his mother away from a Merkava tank, laid her on the ground, and waited for an ambulance to arrive.
 The tank then reversed, running over Safiya with its tracks before his eyes, killing her.
 GBU-39: American-Made Bombs Used in Gaza 
 During the war in Gaza, the Israeli military also deployed American-made GBU-39 bombs in airstrikes targeting homes and urban areas.
 The journalist behind this investigation documented fragments of bombs used by Israeli forces in strikes on homes and tents across Gaza, including the July 2024 attack on Al-Mutannabi School in eastern Khan Younis, which killed 29 Palestinians.
 Daraj presented photographs of the recovered fragments to explosives engineer Mohammed Salem, who identified one metal component as belonging to a GBU-39 precision-guided bomb, also known as the Small Diameter Bomb (SDB), or to its fin-control and mounting assembly.
 According to Salem, the fragment’s identity can be established through the markings printed on its surface. The first line bears the identification number 76301-70P992419-1009 .
 The sequence 70P992419 is a technical part identifier associated with the guidance fins and rear mechanisms of GBU-39 bombs, which adjust the munition’s trajectory during flight.
 The photographs also reveal the manufacturer code MFR 0BSW3 , a Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code registered to Woodward Inc., a supplier of electromechanical systems and guidance actuators to Boeing, the American manufacturer of the bomb.
 Salem added that the markings identify the component’s manufacturing date as March 31, 2022 (2022-03-31).
 According to Salem, Israeli forces used this bomb, designed to penetrate fortified structures, in several attacks that caused mass casualties.
 Among the incidents he cited was the bombing of tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, in July 2025. According to figures released at the time by the Palestinian Ministry of Health, the attack killed 91 Palestinians and wounded 300 others.
 The IAI Harpy: A Loitering Munition 
 Salem also described the IAI Harpy, a one-way attack drone manufactured by Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).
 Designed to remain airborne over operational areas for extended periods and engage targets autonomously, the Harpy combines aerial surveillance capabilities with the destructive power of a tactical missile.
 It can be launched from ground-based platforms or ships without requiring a conventional runway. According to Salem, the aircraft features a two-stroke engine similar to those used in motorcycles and delta-shaped wings.
 The Harpy is among the notable loitering munitions developed by Israel Aerospace Industries, designed to search for and attack targets as a one-way attack drone.
